steps.description: The boy stands hesitant, the Pataka mudra held loosely near the chest (showing awareness/self), with a subtle neck movement (Suka-Ānanā) to glance at the girl.
steps.rasa_expression: Soft, tentative eye contact (Sama Drishthi) followed by a quick, nervous lowering of the gaze.
steps.teaching_note: Utilize a slight, quick weight shift (Kampa) on the heels to show nervous energy while maintaining the Araimandi depth.

steps.description: Takes a deliberate, single step forward (Right foot) on a slight diagonal, transitioning both hands to Katakamukha mudra (indicating focus and preparation).
steps.rasa_expression: A momentary soft focus (Prasanna) in the eyes, showing the decision to approach.
steps.teaching_note: The forward step should be graceful, not stomping (avoid Tattu Mettu); ensure the transition into Katakamukha is smooth.

steps.description: Performs four slow, controlled forward steps (R-L-R-L) using Tripataka mudra in both hands, signaling a graceful approach.
steps.rasa_expression: Gentle, rhythmic Tala (side-to-side neck movement) to show hesitation mixed with sweetness.
steps.teaching_note: Maintain a continuous, even flow throughout the four beats; avoid any upward bounce when stepping forward to sustain the intermediate grace.

steps.description: Stops close to the girl, bringing the right hand in Alapadma (representing the flower) and the left hand to Katakamukha near the chest.
steps.rasa_expression: A slight tilt of the head (Parivrtta Shiras) with a shy, subtle smile.
steps.teaching_note: Hold the Alapadma gently; the flower representation should be held delicately and not too high or low.

steps.description: The right hand holding Alapadma is smoothly and deliberately extended towards the girl (the offer) and held briefly.
steps.rasa_expression: The eyes briefly connect with the hand as it extends, then immediately shift to a humble, downcast gaze (Avahittha) to show shyness.
steps.teaching_note: The extension must be controlled and even; the power of the expression is in the shift of the eye focus immediately following the action.
